0.0.n: Connects the previous discussion to the request that follows.

0.1.n: A polite way to address all the viewers.

0.2.n: Marks the viewers as the people being addressed with this request.

0.4.n: A conversational filler that softens the speaker’s wording.

0.5.n: Refers to comments viewers can post under the video.

0.6.n: Shows the form the suggestions should take: comments.

1.0.n: Works with の to describe the upcoming street interview.

1.1.n: Links 次 to 街頭インタビュー, making it the next street interview.

1.2.n: Describes the public setting of the interview.

1.3.n: An English loanword that combines with 街頭 for interviews conducted on the street.

1.4.n: Links the street interview to 動画, identifying what kind of video it is.

1.5.n: Refers to the upcoming video featuring street interviews.

1.6.n: Marks the video as the setting in which the questions will be asked.

1.8.n: Points to the local residents who will be interviewed.

1.9.n: Refers to people living in the city, rather than emphasizing legal citizenship.

1.10.n: Marks the residents as the people the speaker would ask.

1.11.n: て-form of 聞く + ほしい expresses wanting someone else to act; here, viewers want the speaker to ask.

1.12.n: Turns the preceding phrase into the things viewers want the speaker to ask.

1.13.n: The conditional form of ある; the particle が after こと is omitted in casual speech.

1.14.n: Adds warm encouragement to the request.

1.15.n: て-form of 書く + ください makes a polite request to leave suggestions in the comments.

2.0.n: Signals a transition toward wrapping up the video.

2.3.n: Politely addresses the viewers as a group.

2.4.n: Links 皆さん to コメント, marking the comments as coming from the viewers.

2.5.n: Refers to viewers’ written responses under the video.

2.6.n: Joins comments and likes in the list of viewer actions.

2.8.n: Together with ね, forms いいね, the Japanese label for a social media like.

2.9.n: Adds agreement-seeking warmth to いい; here, the whole expression いいね means a social media like.

2.12.n: An English loanword that combines with 登録 to refer to subscribing to the video channel.

2.13.n: Usually means registration, but チャンネル登録 means subscribing to a channel.

2.14.n: お待ちする is a humble way to say wait; してます shortens しています by dropping い.

3.0.n: Borrowed from Spanish, this gives the farewell a playful feel.

0.lit: So, to everyone, well, as comments,
0.tip: として means as; the speaker starts a request here and completes it in the next line.

1.lit: In the next street interview video, if there are things you want me to ask those residents, please write them.
1.tip: 聞いてほしい means you want someone else to ask, with the speaker understood as that person here.

2.lit: Okay, well then, everyone’s comments and likes, channel subscriptions, I am waiting for.
2.tip: お待ちしてます politely expresses anticipation and serves as a friendly invitation to comment, like, and subscribe.

3.tip: アディオス is Spanish written in katakana, used here as a playful sign-off.
